title: Low Tide: The Samples Wake
statement: Tessera took a core through my section and put a tide in each of seven vials. I have seen what happens to her specimens before: the pressed kelp woke on its sheet, the planted core rooted. So the vials have woken too. Each stopper has a shoot pushing up through it, tallest from the freshest tide at the top of the column and shortest from the seventh, and in the open section the roots that thread between the strata have found the core tube and begun to feel their way into the hole it left. The archive keeps samples; the samples keep growing. It is the same thing that happened to the vessel's core in the other theme, and I think by now it is a rule. The next hand can stopper them harder, which never works.
process: I kept Tessera's section, strata, core tube and the column of seven vials exactly, added a two-leaf shoot growing up through each vial's stopper with height decreasing with depth, and drew rootlets from the strata bending into the core tube's cut.
